title: Scenario Design, Indicators and Triggers
summary: How to build severe but plausible stress scenarios from the firm's own business model, and set early warning indicators and triggers that prompt action in time.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to build severe but plausible stress scenarios from the firm's own business model, and set early warning indicators and triggers that prompt action in time.
Learning Objectives: Design idiosyncratic, market-wide and combined stress scenarios
Use reverse stress testing to identify what would make the business unviable
Set indicators, thresholds and escalation triggers linked to risk appetite
Syllabus: Business model analysis as the starting point for scenarios
Reverse stress testing and points of non-viability
Early warning indicators: capital, liquidity, revenue, client and operational
Calibrating triggers to avoid both false alarms and late action
Intended Audience: Chief financial officers, chief risk officers and finance and treasury teams at investment firms, payment and e-money institutions, crypto-asset service providers and fund managers
Compliance officers, heads of operations and plan owners responsible for drafting and maintaining recovery and wind-down plans
Executive and non-executive directors who approve the plan and would lead the firm through a crisis
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of finance, risk or compliance in a regulated firm is helpful. No prior experience of recovery or wind-down planning is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Key Attributes of Effective Resolution Regimes for Financial Institutions (2014)
Basel Committee, Principles for Sound Liquidity Risk Management and Supervision (2008)
ISO 22301:2019, Security and Resilience – Business Continuity Management Systems
